Epilogue

我取本草之鸿篇，熔铸提炼而为一书。欲起死者而回生，必先活草木金石之朽物。甘草、石斛之属，吾为被以梨园之衣冠，使其歌哭舞蹈于纸上。以活药之力，死者无不速起。即令吾人不必日日用此活药，又安能一日忘之？且共歌舞喧阗，使人人知此药——亦即知其性。
——郭廷选，药性剧序（据英文底本转译；剧本中文题名待核），约1804年
编者说明：题记暂据英文底本转译，尚未见郭廷选序的中文原文，不能视为逐字引文。英文题名为 A Chronicle of Herbs；相关《药会图》《草木传》《本草记》抄本与剧名有复杂的传承关系，不能单凭英语题名确定对应中文版本。所引序文的抄本、确切题名及其年代仍待核。
I combine the grand volumes of
Bencao

, forge and refine them into a book. To lift up the dead and return them to life, I must first enliven the rotten matter of herbs, wood, metal, and stones. For the likes of Licorice and Golden Dendrobium, I dress them in costumes of the theater, and they sing, dance, laugh, and cry onto the paper. With the power of the living drugs, none of the dead will fail to swiftly rise again. Even if we do not use these living drugs every day, how could we ever forget them? Let us dance and sing merrily, so that everyone will know these remedies—that is to say, know their natures.
—Guo Tingxuan, Preface to
A Chronicle of Herbs

凶悍有毒的番邦兵马进犯中原。老成持重的甘草大臣主张议和，勇猛无畏的大黄将军力主迎战。敌军掳走了甘草美丽的女儿菊花；快腿信使栀子把她的求救讯息传回家乡。年少气盛的石斛武士救出菊花，并娶她为妻。最后，百药之王人参设下盛宴，为新人及忠臣庆功。这部短剧出自华中开业医者郭廷选（约1804年在世）之手，以药典人物搬演人间悲欢。与先前文士所作的“药性剧”不同，郭廷选希望这部教化剧能尽可能接触广大的观众。拟人化的药物在台上欢歌起舞，它们生动的表演促使观者省思自身的性情。

Fierce, toxic troops of foreign origin descend on the Central Kingdom. Licorice, the venerated minister, tries to negotiate peace, but rhubarb, the fearless general, advocates fighting back. The enemy captures chrysanthemum, licorice’s beautiful daughter; gardenia, the swift-legged messenger, relays her call for help back home. Golden Dendrobium, the brash youthful warrior, rescues chrysanthemum and marries her. In the end, ginseng, emperor of all medicine, hosts a grand banquet to honor the newlyweds and his faithful officials. The plot of this short play written by Guo Tingxuan (fl. 1804), a physician practicing in central China, reenacts human dramas with characters drawn from the pharmacopeia. Departing from previous “pharmaceutical dramas” composed by literati authors, Guo intended for his didactic show to reach as wide an audience as possible. The anthropomorphized medicinal drugs “sing and dance merrily” on stage, their lively performance encouraging viewers to reflect on their own natures.
本草药典的编纂早已从国家赞助的文化舞台上退场，但药物物性的力量仍以不那么集中化的形式延续。直到二十世纪初，郭廷选的剧本依然流行，许多地方改编本以手抄形式保存下来。
十九世纪下半叶，清廷——多少有些像剧中重构的隐喻王国——面临内忧外患的严峻挑战，郭廷选道德讯息的迫切性也因此获得了新的意义。药学文化的通俗化，映照出太平天国战争（1852—64）与亚罗号战争（1856—60）创伤之后，地方社会重夺道德主体性的种种努力。
药师与本地士绅、僧道以及日益壮大的儒者行动者联合起来，重建地方社会，重塑国家政治。围绕药性权威的争夺，继续为现代中国知识、权力与伦理之间的复杂互动提供线索；药学仍然是观察人们持久寻求如何从政治上治理人性这一共识的良好视角。

The making of the bencao pharmacopeia had long faded from the government-sponsored cultural stage, but the power of pharmaceutical objecthood endured in less centralized expressions. As late as the early twentieth century, Guo’s play remained popular with many local adaptations preserved in hand-copied manuscripts.

The urgency of Guo’s moral message took on new meanings during the second half of the nineteenth century as the Qing state, resembling more or less the metaphorical kingdom reconstructed in the play, faced serious challenges from both internal and external threats. The popularization of pharmaceutical culture mirrored the efforts of local communities’ efforts to reclaim moral agency in the wake of the traumatic Taiping Wars (1852–64) and the Arrow War (1856–60).

Pharmacists joined forces with resident gentry, clergy, and a growing contingent of Confucian activists to rebuild local society and reshape national politics. The struggle for authority over the nature of drugs continues to shed light on the complex interplay among knowledge, power, and ethics in modern China; pharmacy remains a good vantage point from which to observe the perennial search for consensus over the political administration of human nature.

1844年8月24日，第一次鸦片战争（1839—42）中清中国败于英国之后，一个法国使团抵达澳门。继中英《南京条约》之后，法国人与清朝官员谈判，于同年10月签订了类似的《黄埔条约》，获得在新开条约口岸通商与居留的特权。使团访问宁波、上海等口岸期间，随团医生梅尔基奥尔-奥诺雷·伊万（Melchior-Honoré Yvan，1803—73）考察了当地药铺，归国后根据观察发表了一篇关于药材贸易的记述。伊万观察到，中国药师在中国社会中“作为科学人士、作为商人”扮演着关键角色，占有“在此文明中颇为重要”的地位。然而，在伊万眼中，这个文明仍然如此“停滞”，以至于一家小店就能容纳“天朝全境所有事物的完整标本”。
伊万写作的1847年，欧洲本身即将被卷入又一轮革命狂热；他急于借这部关于中国的出版物来确保自己作为科学人士的地位。

On August 24, 1844, a French delegation arrived in Macau in the wake of Qing China’s defeat by Great Britain during the First Opium War (1839–42). Following the Sino-British Treaty of Nanjing, the French negotiated with Qing officials and signed a comparable Treaty of Whampoa in October that year, which granted France privileges of trading and residing in the newly opened treaty ports. During the delegation’s visit to some of these ports, including Ningbo and Shanghai, the accompanying physician, Dr. Melchior-Honoré Yvan (1803–73), visited local pharmacies there and, upon his return, published an account of the pharmaceutical trade according to his observations. The Chinese pharmacist, observed Yvan, plays a crucial role in Chinese society “as man of science, as merchant” and occupies a place “of importance with this civilization.” Yet, in Yvan’s eyes, this civilization remained so “stationary” that a small shop could contain the “complete specimen of what exists in all the extent of the Celestial Empire.”
Writing in 1847, when Europe herself was about to be swept into another round of revolutionary zeal, Yvan was keen to use this publication on China to secure his own status as a man of science.

至此，我希望本书已令人信服地证明，药学在中国历史上的“科学、工业与社会”生活中具有重要作用。然而，我们今天的预设与伊万不同：在我们看来，把那个文明视为动态过程而非静态实体，能让我们学到更多。即便如此，伊万的报告仍充满富有启发性的细节，我希望读者读到这里已对这些细节感到熟悉。他在宁波药铺中目睹的中国“药物消费量之大”——那些店铺以精致服务堪比当时法国“最气派的药材行”——对赵学敏来说想必并不陌生；仅仅数十年前，赵学敏还在这座城市里打听白胡椒的本性。伊万还注意到，从宁波到东南亚马六甲的中国药铺，都共享同样的“陈设与布置方式”，这证实了中国商业网络在跨区域与海外的延伸。
他在新加坡遇到的中国企业家，夸耀自己掌握种植儿茶钩藤、提取富含单宁的儿茶的秘技；这是一项利润丰厚的贸易。
这些人难道不是中国腹地“种植场”主人的同道吗？在那里，厚朴与黄连正是被当作“野生”药材栽培的。这些难道都只是一个停滞文明、凝固于时间之中的表现吗？回看本书开头展示的中国药铺微缩模型（图0.1），读者现在或许会有不同的答案。

By now, I hope this book has made a compelling case for the usefulness of pharmacy in “scientific, industrial, and social” life in Chinese history. Our assumptions today, however, differ from Yvan’s in that we learn much more by seeing that civilization as a dynamic process, not static entities. Yet even so, Yvan’s report brims with revealing details that should, I hope, sound familiar at this point. The “enormous consumption of drugs” in China that he witnessed in the pharmacies of Ningpo—establishments that matched in their exquisite service the “grandest shops of droguerie” in contemporary France—would have been familiar to Zhao Xuemin, who had inquired after the nature of white pepper in that city only a few decades earlier. Yvan also noted that Chinese pharmacies from Ningpo to Malacca in Southeast Asia shared the same “provisions and mode of arrangement,” confirming the interregional and overseas extension of Chinese mercantile networks.

The Chinese entrepreneurs he encountered in Singapore boasted secret techniques for cultivating the shrub gambier and extracting the tannin-rich substance known as catechu, a profitable venue of trade.

Were they not peers of the owners of “plantations” in China’s own hinterland, where magnolia barks and Golden Thread were cultivated as “wild” medicine? Are these all but manifestations of a motionless civilization, frozen in time? Looking back at the miniature model of the Chinese pharmacy presented at the beginning of this book (figure 0.1), one might now have a different answer.
自十六世纪晚期起，樟树这个不起眼的小镇便确立为重要的“药码头”；樟树人想必熟悉伊万所描述的贸易世界。在十九世纪动荡的历史中，樟树商人及各商帮中的同行总体上都过得不错。直到1930年代，樟树与祁州的庙会仍能吸引七八万顾客；而外国势力的广泛经营，实际上还帮助本地药师在条约口岸开店，并把立足点扩展到香港、东南亚乃至世界各地。
他们新得的财富，提示出另一种关于中国晚帝制时代的叙事，并不像通常设想的那样失败主义。尽管今日樟树精心建构了种种“传统”故事，樟树人的历史，与二十世纪之交城市中拔地而起的大医院一样，同属于全球医学的现代史。无论战时还是平时，中国都持续向世界供应大量药材原料，其中许多采自旧帝国边疆地区。
尽管这个故事尚待讲述，我希望本书已把当代中国商人、医者与科学家锚定在一个生机勃勃的政治与科学传统之中。

The people of Zhangshu, the modest town that established itself as the important “medicinal wharf” beginning in the late sixteenth century, would have been familiar with the world of trade described by Yvan. Throughout the turbulent history of the nineteenth century, Zhangshu merchants and their counterparts in different merchant companies fared quite well overall. Up to the 1930s, market fairs held in Zhangshu and Qizhou enjoyed attendance of 70,000–80,000 customers, and the extensive operations of foreign interests, in fact, helped local pharmacists set up shops in the treaty ports and expand their foothold in Hong Kong, Southeast Asia, and all over the world.

Their newfound fortunes suggest a less defeatist narrative of China’s late imperial era than is commonly assumed. Despite the carefully constructed tales of “tradition” in today’s Zhangshu, the story of its people belongs to a modern history of global medicine as much as the grand hospitals being erected in cities at the turn of the twentieth century. In war and in peace, China continued to supply large quantities of raw pharmaceutical materials to the world, much of which had been harvested from the former empire’s frontier regions.

Though this is a story yet to be told, I hope that the present study has served to anchor the merchants, physicians, and scientists of contemporary China in a lively political and scientific tradition.

在本书中，我追踪了1500至1800年间中国药物物性知识的变迁轨迹。我们从文化再生产的过程不再仰望帝国中心寻求指引之时开始，见证了晚明这一去中心化进程所释放出的惊人表达多样性。我们追随那些最热切的尝试：重新发明本草，建立一门可靠的自然之学，进而作为道德行动的基础。我们看到，士人业余主义在内有王朝危机、外有医药市场抵制的双重夹击下败下阵来。最后，我们剖析了盛清国家强行重新分类知识、把药物事务委托给商业行动者的种种偶然过程。自清中叶起，两条分岔的道路发展起来，各自通向不同的未来；在那些未来中，本草药典的幽灵将被唤回人世。

In this book, I have traced the trajectory of change in Chinese knowledge of pharmaceutical objecthood between 1500 and 1800. We began when the processes of cultural reproduction no longer looked to an imperial center for guidance, and witnessed the amazing variety of expressions this decentralizing process unleashed in late Ming times. We followed the most zealous attempts to reinvent bencao and establish a reliable science of nature that could, in turn, serve as a basis for moral action. We saw the defeat of literati amateurism by both dynastic crisis and resistance from the medical marketplace. Finally, we parsed the contingent processes through which the High Qing state forcefully reclassified knowledge and delegated pharmaceutical matters to mercantile actors. Beginning in mid-Qing times, two divergent paths developed, each leading to different futures in which the phantoms of bencao pharmacopeia would be called back to life.
其中一条道路，通向以现代科学家与医学专业人士为代表的、以科学为基础的行动主义复兴；他们坚持认为，自己对自然的优越理解，足以证成其通往权力的道路。1930年，在哈佛受训的医生、中华民国卫生部长刘瑞恒（Liu Jui-heng，1890—1961）主持编纂的第一部现代药典《中华药典》颁布。按照他的构想，药典只应收录符合当时国际标准的物质。
这种做法体现了科学家与医生试图从民国政府与现代大学的崇高讲坛上重建知识与权力统一的努力；这一普遍主义举动，植根于新儒家在格物中求道德的追求。

One of these paths led to a revival of science-based activism in the figures of modern scientists and medical professionals who insisted that their own privileged understanding of nature justified their paths to power. In 1930, the first modern pharmacopeia was published under the supervision of the Harvard-trained doctor and Minister of Health of the Republic of China, Liu Jui-heng (1890–1961). According to his vision, the pharmacopeia was to include only substances congruent with the international standard of the day.

This approach exemplified the attempt on the part of scientists and medical doctors to establish a new unity of knowledge and power from the high altars of the republican government and the modern universities, a universalist move rooted in the neo-Confucian search for morality in the investigation of things.
Editor's note (Chinese): 有关《中华药典》1930年颁布、1931年对外发售的日期，研究资料记载不一；此处保留1930年颁布，具体发售日期及作者所据版本原件尚待核实。
在这一精神的裹挟下，新一代科学家誓言用化学分析的现代工具使中药现代化。在日本受训的年轻药理学家赵燏黄，访问祁州一年一度的庙会（当年倒霉的智天豹曾在那里编造星象预言），试图确认市场所售药材的植物学与化学身份。
1930至40年代，赵燏黄积极投身于利用本土植物资源制造药物的爱国热潮。这一对传统进行科学转化的谱系延续至今。中药研究与本草文献领域的领军学者郑金生教授，1970年代又受教于赵氏的一位学生。

Swept along in this spirit, a new generation of scientists vowed to modernize Chinese materia medica with the modern tools of chemical analysis. Zhao Yuhuang, a young pharmacologist trained in Japan, visited the annual market fair in Qizhou (where the hapless Zhi Tianbao had once hatched his astrological prophecy) and attempted to ascertain the botanical and chemical identities of medicinal substances on sale there.

Zhao was actively involved in the patriotic rush to manufacture pharmaceuticals using native botanical resources during the 1930s and 1940s. This lineage of scientific transformation of tradition continues today. Professor Zheng Jinsheng, a leading scholar on Chinese materia medica research and the bencao literature was, in turn, trained by one of Zhao’s students in the 1970s.
沿着第二条道路，本土医学正统的捍卫者抵抗科学无所不包的力量，迅速聚集在“中式”与“西式”药物之本体差异的旗帜下——这一说法实际上是对人性的一种特殊主义解读。本体分歧的话语最早出现在晚清中西医“会通”论者那里，并在甲午战争之后及1911年革命期间高涨的民族主义中积蓄势头。
现代传统主义者动员民族主义情感，主张中国人绝不能与浸润着中国文化的中国药物相割裂。药师们则谨慎行事，把自己塑造成一种既现代化、又本质上属于中国的企业的代表。

Following a second path and resisting the all-encompassing power of science, defenders of native medical orthodoxy quickly rallied around the ontological difference between “Chinese” and “Western” drugs—a statement that amounted to a particularist reading of human nature. The discourse of ontological divergence first appeared in late Qing synthesizers (
huitong
) of Chinese and Western medicine and picked up momentum in the aftermath of the first Sino-Japanese War and surging nationalism during the 1911 Revolution.

Mobilizing nationalist sentiments, the modern traditionalists argued that Chinese people must never be severed from Chinese remedies steeped in Chinese culture. Pharmacists toed a cautious line by posing themselves as representatives of a modernized, yet quintessentially Chinese, business.
中医（Zhongyi）或国医（guoyi）与西医（xiyi）倡导者之间的首次公开冲突，发生在1920年代末至1930年代；最终，国民政府内部倾向改革的领导人未能压过传统捍卫者。双方达成妥协：两种医学实践体系及其药物储备将在现代中国的国家建设进程中并存、共同演化；历史学家把这一结果戏称为“杂种医学”（mongrel medicine）。
中国共产党以强烈的反美民族主义纲领赢得1949年内战，拥护传统的疗效。1963年版《中华人民共和国药典》修订时，首次把传统中药（zhongyao）与“西药”（xiyao）分卷收录。
迟至2013年，中国才把各监管机构合并为国家食品药品监督管理总局（CFDA）。界定与监管这套双重医疗体系的任务，在后勤上仍具挑战性，在政治上仍然复杂。

The first open clash between advocates of Chinese medicine (
Zhongyi
) or national medicine (
guoyi
) against Western medicine (
xiyi

) took place in the late 1920s and 1930s, and in the end the reform-minded leaders within the nationalist government could not prevail over the defenders of tradition. A compromise was reached in which the two systems of medical practice, along with their pharmaceutical repertoires, would coexist and coevolve in the state-building process of modern China, a result that historians have dubbed “mongrel medicine.”

The Chinese Communist Party, winning the civil war in 1949 under a strong anti-American nationalist platform, espoused the efficacy of tradition. In 1963, the People’s Republic of China revised its official pharmacopeia to include, for the first time, traditional materia medica (
zhongyao
) in a separate volume from “Western drugs” (
xiyao

As recently as in 2013, China consolidated its regulatory offices into one Food and Drug Administration (CFDA). The task of defining and regulating the dual system of health care remains logistically challenging and politically complicated.

自1970年代以来，中国制度化的中医在争议声中获得越来越多的国际认可。
世界各地以实践为导向的利益群体，重新激活了对中国医学传统的学术研究，把它视为生物医学之外的一种替代疗法。与晚明出版市场颇为相似，在中医倡导者的强劲需求下，大量此前冷僻的文本——许多成于明清时期——被发掘并重新出版。本书在某种程度上也得益于这场出版热潮。与此同时，更高的曝光度也使中医因滥用有毒物质、虐待动物及其他环境问题等伦理争议而声名不佳。
如今，每当中医地位的争论在现实生活或网络上爆发，交锋很快就会沿着普遍主义与文化民族主义之间的断层线升级为政治分歧。如果我们现在能够同意，任何文明——无论中国还是其他——都不存在铁板一块的科学传统，那么研究这许多过去与许多传统的目的，就是为未来创造新的规范、规程与叙事。
Since the 1970s, the institutionalized form of TCM in China has gained more and more international recognition amid much controversy.

Practice-oriented interests all over the world have rejuvenated the academic study of the Chinese medical tradition as an alternative mode of therapeutics to biomedicine. Somewhat parallel to the late Ming publishing market, a large number of previously obscure texts, many of which dated to Ming-Qing times, were discovered and republished thanks to a robust demand from TCM advocates. This study has benefited, to some extent, from that publishing boom. At the same time, enhanced publicity also made TCM notorious for ethical issues involving the abuse of toxic substances, animal abuse, and other environmental concerns.

Today, each time a debate over the status of TCM erupts in real life or online, the exchanges quickly escalate into political disagreements along the fault line between universalism and cultural nationalism. If we can now agree that there was no monolithic scientific tradition in any one civilization—Chinese or otherwise—then the goal of investigating these many pasts and many traditions is to create new norms, protocols, and narratives for the future.

与郭廷选一样，我熔铸提炼本草巨著以撰成此书，但并非为了教化。当下不是任何形式怀旧的时刻：我既不想呼唤唐宋国家赞助药典的二十一世纪翻版，也不想沉湎于这样的推测——若非清军入关成功，中国是否可能在十七世纪发生科学革命。至此或许已经清楚，我终究是有立场的：相比于《中庸》板着面孔的告诫，我在《大学》给人力量的讯息中找到更多慰藉——它相信，一个人内在的道德行动能力，必须以格物所得的知识为基础。更重要的是，这个“知”的人可以是任何投身于此一旅程的人，而不只是少数命定之人。通过激活推动这部药物物性史的各类立场，我希望避免以中国传统与（西方）现代性之间的虚假二分来思考。知药，即知我们自己。

Like Guo Tingxuan, I “forge and refine” the “grand volumes of bencao” to compose the present book, but not for didactical purposes. The present is no time for nostalgia of any kind: I do not wish to call for a twenty-first-century replica of the Tang-Song state-sponsored pharmacopeia, nor indulge in speculations as to whether China could have had a scientific revolution in the seventeenth century had the Qing conquest not been successful. It may be apparent by now that I do, after all, have a position to take: compared to the stern-faced admonitions of the
Doctrine of the Mean
, I find more consolation in the empowering message of
Great Learning

, which is to believe that a person’s innate capacity for moral action must be grounded by knowledge gleaned from the investigation of things. More importantly, this knowing person can be anyone who applies themselves to this journey, not just a preordained few. By activating the full spectrum of positions that motivated this history of pharmaceutical objecthood, I hope to avoid thinking in terms of the false dichotomy between Chinese tradition and (Western) modernity. To know our remedies is to know ourselves.
